name: MD5 Hash Generator
description: Generate the MD5 checksum of any text instantly, entirely in your browser — useful for cache keys, file-integrity spot checks, and legacy system compatibility.

faq.question: Is MD5 secure?
faq.answer: No — MD5 is cryptographically broken. Collisions (two different inputs producing the same hash) can be generated deliberately, so MD5 must never be used for passwords, digital signatures, or anything security-critical. It's still widely used for non-adversarial checksums: verifying a download wasn't corrupted, deduplicating files, or generating a cache key. Use SHA-256 or SHA-512 for anything security-sensitive.

faq.question: Why does the same text always produce the same hash?
faq.answer: MD5 is deterministic — the same input bytes always produce the same 128-bit output. That's what makes it useful as a checksum: hash a file before and after a transfer, and if the hashes match, the bytes are (almost certainly) identical.

faq.question: Does this match the MD5 output of command-line tools like md5sum?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as the input bytes match. This tool hashes the UTF-8 encoding of whatever text you type, which is what md5sum would hash if you piped the same text to it without a trailing newline.
